description: Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.

c.request: Looking at what has actually been rented (each rental traced through its inventory copy to the film, skipping any that don't link up), what share of the rented films does each film `rating` account for, out of the total across all ratings? For the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, give one row with: their combined number of rented films, their average share, and how far on average their share sits above that average share. No rounding. Each rating's share is its number of rental transactions as a fraction of all rental transactions.
c.sql:
WITH rating_rentals AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) as cnt
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
shares AS (
  SELECT rating, cnt, cnt / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM rating_rentals) as share
  FROM rating_rentals
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT cnt, share
  FROM shares
  WHERE share > (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(cnt) as combined_rented_films,
  AVG(share) as average_share,
  AVG(share) - (SELECT AVG(share) FROM shares) as average_above_average
FROM above_avg

a.request: Link each rental to its inventory copy and that copy's film, dropping rentals with no matching copy or film. For each film `rating`, count the rental transactions, so a film rented many times counts each time. Compute each rating's share as its count divided by the total of these counts across all ratings. Keep only the ratings whose share is above the average share across ratings, with each rating weighted equally. Return a single row with: the total count of those ratings, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that average share. Do not round anything.
a.sql: WITH rental_film AS (SELECT f.rating FROM rental r INNER JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id INNER JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id), rating_counts AS (SELECT rating, COUNT(*) as rental_count FROM rental_film GROUP BY rating), total_rentals AS (SELECT SUM(rental_count) as total_count FROM rating_counts), rating_shares AS (SELECT rating, rental_count, rental_count * 1.0 / (SELECT total_count FROM total_rentals) as share FROM rating_counts), average_share_calc AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM rating_shares), filtered_ratings AS (SELECT rs.rental_count, rs.share FROM rating_shares rs CROSS JOIN average_share_calc asc WHERE rs.share > asc.avg_share) SELECT SUM(rental_count) as total_count, AVG(share) as average_share, AVG(share - (SELECT avg_share FROM average_share_calc)) as avg_excess FROM filtered_ratings

b.request: Calculate each film rating's share as its proportion of total rental transactions; identify ratings with above-average shares; for those ratings, report their combined rental count, the mean of their shares, and the average amount each share exceeds the overall mean share.
b.sql:
WITH rating_rentals AS (
  SELECT 
    f.rating,
    COUNT(r.rental_id) AS rental_count
  FROM rental r
  JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
  JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
total_rentals AS (
  SELECT SUM(rental_count) AS total FROM rating_rentals
),
shares AS (
  SELECT 
    rental_count,
    rental_count * 1.0 / (SELECT total FROM total_rentals) AS share
  FROM rating_rentals
),
avg_share_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS mean_share
  FROM shares
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT s.rental_count, s.share, a.mean_share
  FROM shares s
  CROSS JOIN avg_share_calc a
  WHERE s.share > a.mean_share
)
SELECT
  SUM(rental_count) AS combined_rental_count,
  AVG(share) AS mean_share,
  AVG(share - mean_share) AS avg_share_excess
FROM above_avg
b.raw: Calculate each film rating's share as its proportion of total rental transactions; identify ratings with above-average shares; for those ratings, report their combined rental count, the mean of their shares, and the average amount each share exceeds the overall mean share.

d.request: For each film rating, calculate the proportion of all rental transactions that involve films with that rating; identify ratings with above-average proportion; for those above-average ratings combined, report the total number of rental transactions, their mean proportion, and the mean excess of their proportions above the overall mean proportion.
d.sql: WITH rental_by_rating AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS rental_count FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON r.inventory_id = i.inventory_id JOIN film f ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), total_rentals AS (SELECT SUM(rental_count) AS total FROM rental_by_rating), proportions AS (SELECT rbr.rating, rbr.rental_count, rbr.rental_count / tr.total AS proportion FROM rental_by_rating rbr CROSS JOIN total_rentals tr), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(proportion) AS mean_prop FROM proportions) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN p.proportion > om.mean_prop THEN p.rental_count ELSE 0 END) AS total_transactions, AVG(CASE WHEN p.proportion > om.mean_prop THEN p.proportion ELSE NULL END) AS mean_proportion, AVG(CASE WHEN p.proportion > om.mean_prop THEN p.proportion - om.mean_prop ELSE NULL END) AS mean_excess FROM proportions p CROSS JOIN overall_mean om;
